messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finpay.com>, Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: routing segmentation, quotas & guardrails (FinPay)

Hi Liam / Sara —

Thanks again for the call today. Wanted to capture what we heard and confirm next steps so we keep momentum. TL;DR: main pain is unpredictable per-customer spikes causing downstream cost and an inability to enforce premium vs standard entitlements at the routing layer.

Key pain points you shared:
- Burstiness from a handful of premium customers that ruins your shared pool economics (observed spike patterns 3–4x baseline during payroll cycles).
- No simple way today to define per-customer soft/hard limits across routes; engineering builds are ad-hoc and slow.
- Need deterministic behavior during capacity constraints: which customers get throttled, which are routed to slower-but-cheaper models, and which get queued/failover.
- Audit and billing alignment — you must correlate observed throttle events with invoice line items.

Current stack (as described):
- Fronted by internal request proxy -> shared LLM cluster (mixed workloads) -> homegrown quota service.
- Limited telemetry on per-request model variant selection; billing is aggregated at the service level.

Success criteria you called out:
1) Ability to enforce per-customer rate ceilings and burst windows (configurable per-customer).
2) Per-route policies to prefer lower-cost variants automatically when budget thresholds or capacity signals trigger.
3) Observable, auditable events that map throttle/reroute decisions to customer billing records.
4) Low risk rollout path: canary by customer segment + automatic fallback to a safe variant.

What Redwood proposes for a PoC (high level):
- Short (4-week) POC with a small cohort of customers (2 premium, 3 standard): ship a policy layer that implements per-customer soft/hard limits, per-route fallback rules, and emits events for billing.
- Provide a config UI and REST API for quick rule changes.
- Run a 72-hour canary with traffic mirroring before cutover.
- Deliver a short runbook for incident response (how to adjust limits, failover steps).

Risks & open questions we need from you:
- Confirmation of the customer cohort for the PoC and their expected traffic profile (avg qps, typical peak).
- Any regulatory constraints around routing decisions (must not send certain PII to third-party models).
- Target SLA/latency budget for premium customers under degraded conditions. You mentioned ~100ms p95 as a goal — confirm.

Next steps (proposed):
1) You share the PoC cohort and weekly traffic samples (by Thu Oct 9).
2) Redwood to share a short draft policy config + implementation plan (attached) by Fri Oct 10.
3) Align on a 1-week mirror/canary window + start date during the week of Oct 19.

Attaching draft: redwood-routes-and-quotas-draft.pdf (policy template + example configs) and a proposed PoC schedule (finpay-poc-schedule.xlsx).

If this matches your view, I'll file these items into the HubSpot deal and we can get legal looped if needed for a quick SOW.

Thanks — look forward to your confirmation.

Best,
Rafael
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: routing segmentation, quotas & guardrails (FinPay)

Rafael — thanks for the thorough summary, this looks accurate. A few clarifications from our side:

- Confirmed: 100ms p95 is the target for premium under normal load; during degradations we accept higher tail latency but expect deterministic fallback (i.e., reroute to cheaper model rather than timeouts).
- PoC cohort suggestion: 2 premium customers (PayStream & PayrollPro) and 3 standard midsize merchants (sample list attached in a separate note). We'll send you anonymized traffic histograms by Thursday.
- Compliance: we cannot route anything with bank account numbers to third-party hosted models. Any routing policy must include a tag-based exclusion rule.

Also appreciate the audit event mapping — that is critical for our billing ops.

Agree to the proposed timeline. One ask: can you add a short section in the PoC runbook about how billing reconciliation keys are emitted so our finance team can validate invoices?

I'll confirm cohort names + histograms by Thu.

Thanks,
Liam
Head of Platform Engineering | FinPay
liam.oconnor@finpay.com
